notes:
Summary: Moonwell (consumer fintech, 300 employees) evaluating Redwood for customer support automation. Primary goals: reduce AHT via real-time agent assist, automated ticket summarization, and reliable tool-calling (Zendesk + internal ops tools). Strong emphasis on RAG over internal KBs with citation provenance and recency controls.

Key requirements / constraints:
- Workloads: low-latency agent assist (p95 target < 400ms for step-by-step suggestion), bulk nightly embedding index for freshness, ticket summarization for compliance.
- Spikes: x8-10 traffic during product launches / promo events; must degrade gracefully (canary -> smaller model -> cached responses).
- Retrieval: multi-source (confluence, KB, transcripts, product changelogs), need source-level citations + hit-level freshness windows.
- Integrations: Zendesk + ServiceNow for tool-calling, SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, audit logs forwarded to Splunk.
- Security: SOC2 + ISO27001 required, KMS integration mandatory, data residency in US and EU for EU customers. Retention controls (1y default, negotiable).

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-11-20: inbound from engineering blog; AE outreach by Sofia.
- 2025-12-08: discovery call (ff_2026-02-18_7532 referenced) -- landed on POC scope: Dedicated capacity for latency testing + RAG prototype.
- 2026-01-15: security kickoff; provided initial security FAQ (drive link).
- 2026-02-01: infra kickoff; SE (Lukas) proposed topology: VPC private control plane + dedicated GPU pool.
- 2026-02-18: POC deep-dive (ff_2026-02-18_7532).
- 2026-03-02: live POC run 1 (throughput bench, RED-4521 ticket opened for perf anomaly).

POC deliverables / milestones:
- Week 0: ingest 18 months of KB + recent changelogs; build embeddings and vector index.
- Week 2: RAG QA baseline: precision/recall on citation tasks; implement citation overlay with source links.
- Week 4: latency bench on Dedicated nodes w/ batching; validate p95 < 400ms at 50 concurrent agents.
- Optional: failover policy test (dedicated -> hosted fallback) and cost trade-off report from Redwood Optimize.

Quotes / notes from stakeholders:
- CTO (Amit Rao): "We need explicit citations in agent suggestions — compliance will not accept hallucinated answers."
- Head of Support (Maya Singh): "Summaries must be short, auditable, and include ticket IDs referenced."

Technical concerns raised by internal team:
- How to keep citations fresh when product docs change daily? (update cadence + incremental re-embedding).
- Retrieval ranking across heterogeneous sources (confluence vs transcript store) — wants reranker + provenance scoring.
- Cost sensitivity: wants a clear unit-cost tradeoff graph (dedicated vs hosted) for expected 10M tokens/month.

Open security / procurement items:
- Provide data residency attestation for EU customers (requested 2026-02-20).
- KMS/HSM integration plan and audit log retention spec (SEC-1103).
- SSO test window: 2 week window needed for enterprise SAML testing.

Next steps (short):
- SE to deliver latency test config + synthetic load script by 2026-03-12 (in progress).
- AE to circulate draft SOW and pricing (target: 2026-03-18).
- Security to send final attestation template for legal review.

Decision factors for Moonwell:
- Proof that Redwood can provide: deterministic citations, freshness controls, graceful spike handling, and predictable per-token economics.
- Preference for Dedicated or Private if security answers are satisfactory; else hybrid with hosted fallback.

Linked artifacts: drive/security FAQ, call recordings (fireflies ids), RED-4521 for perf, SEC-1103 security follow-up.

Sales shorthand / internal notes:
- Warm account, CTO engaged, procurement expected after POC if perf & security checks pass.
- Price sensitivity but willing to pay for stable p95 and clear audit trail.
- "If you can show citation fidelity and spike reliability, high chance to move to Dedicated commit (6-12mo)."
